The driver constructs the headless Chat without throttle:50, because throttle is a react useChat-wrapper option that does not exist on the headless ChatInit type — the task's 'throttle 50 driven headlessly' is not literally expressible at the class level.

The driver loads ai/@ai-sdk/react and the hook module through computed specifiers bounded by local structural interfaces rather than static or type-only imports, because any static import of apps/example package types injects global DOM augmentations into the root tsc program and breaks unrelated spec files.

AC-1's record tally and 'new request ID distinct from the failed one' were satisfied as cross-capture evidence rather than in-run assertions (see findings), matching the oracle ORI-RN-004's reviewed web leg actually implemented.
concerns: The state damage is a throttling race and varies run to run: my final RED capture happened to fail via the stale-streaming-itemId class (0 duplicated itemIds in that body), so the duplication-class RED shape exists only in the cycle-1 probe captures (.tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/cycle-1/probe-duplication.ts output) — a future SDK upgrade could change the damage shape into a third class the sanitize does not cover.
The retry's deltaCount >= 2 oracle rides on the 'Reply with the single word pineapple.' prompt empirically streaming as 2 text deltas; a provider-side chunking change to 1 delta would flake GREEN.

The cast at apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts:49 (init as Parameters<typeof expoFetch>[1]) papers over undici-RequestInit vs expo-FetchRequestInit typing-lib skew and would silently conceal a future real signature divergence.

The pre-commit biome job is vacuous in this environment ('pnpm lint' dies with 'Linter process terminated abnormally' yet exits 0), so hook-level lint coverage here rests on the direct-binary verification I recorded, not on the gate itself.

Keep-first semantics mean that if a future damage ordering ever places a partial snapshot before the complete one for the same itemId, the partial text is what gets sent — contract-prescribed and provider-accepted, but lower history fidelity.
findings: The defect is two failure classes, not one: duplicated assistant entries repeating itemIds AND unique-but-stale itemIds from streams that never completed, where the second class returns OpenAI 400 'Item with id … not found' even with zero duplicates — proven by direct provider replay in .tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/cycle-1/diag-raw-provider-error.ts, and invisible in server records because sanitizeError collapses every provider failure to one generic string (apps/example/server/chat.ts:162).

Mechanism: @ai-sdk/openai responses defaults store to true and converts every assistant text part carrying providerMetadata.openai.itemId into a bare item_reference whose content is NOT sent (apps/example/node_modules/@ai-sdk/openai/src/responses/convert-to-openai-responses-input.ts:606-610), so a stale itemId simultaneously drops the partial text and fails the request.

The client-side staleness signal is part.state: aborted turns leave text parts stuck at 'streaming' while completed turns end 'done' — this is what the sanitize keys on and it is the only reliable client-side discriminator.

The minimal AC-1 scenario as written (seed turn, stop backend, submit, restart, retry) does NOT reproduce the failure — a single completed turn plus endpoint loss retries successfully even pre-fix; an aborted mid-stream turn (or equivalent state damage) between them is the prerequisite, which is why the driver adds the aborted-essay leg.

Static or even type-only imports of apps/example modules (the hook via expo/fetch, and the ai/@ai-sdk/react dist d.ts themselves) add global DOM augmentations (HTMLElement | SVGElement unions) to the root tsc program and break unrelated spec files — any future driver touching these packages must runtime-load via computed specifiers with structural surfaces.

The published expo/fetch entry (expo/fetch.js requiring ./src/winter/fetch/index) cannot resolve in plain Node at all; only Metro resolves it, and its types live under expo/build/winter/fetch — which is why the lazy-import enabler works for types but must never be called headlessly.

Terminal-status helpers must gate on status DEPARTURE before waiting for the terminal state, because Chat sets 'submitted' asynchronously after sendMessage returns and a naive wait returns the stale 'ready' (a vacuous pass that bit the first driver draft).

feedback: The RED must_observe pinned the duplicated-itemIds shape, but which failure class manifests is a throttling race — write the RED bar as 'real provider rejection with an error record and 0 deltas' (both classes satisfy it) and treat the specific payload shape as captured-not-required.
